result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.is_k_regular()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if the graph is k-regular (all nodes have degree `k`). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L4651-L4722){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.is_k_regular(k) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A graph is k-regular if every node has degree exactly `k`. For directed graphs, this means all nodes have in-degree `k` and out-degree `k`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [k]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The degree value to check for. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the graph is k-regular, `False` otherwise. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} This is the stricter cousin of `is_regular()`: instead of asking "is every degree equal?", it pins down the exact value $k$. Empty graphs vacuously satisfy $k = 0$; cycles are $2$-regular; the complete graph $K_n$ is $(n - 1)$-regular; and paths are never regular because their endpoints have degree $1$ while interior nodes have degree $2$. On directed graphs the check tightens to both $\deg^-(v) = k$ and $\deg^+(v) = k$ for every $v$. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A cycle's nodes each have degree `2`, so it satisfies `k=2` but no other value of `k`: ::: {#f16e27e7 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_cycle_graph(6) graph.is_k_regular(2), graph.is_k_regular(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (True, False) ``` ::: ::: A complete graph `K_n` is `(n-1)`-regular, so it satisfies `k = n - 1` but not `k = n`: ::: {#ee70c67d .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() n = 5 for i in range(n): graph.add_node(label=f"n{i}") nodes = sorted(graph.get_node_ids()) for i in range(n): for j in range(i + 1, n): graph.add_edge(nodes[i], nodes[j]) graph.is_k_regular(n - 1), graph.is_k_regular(n) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (True, False) ``` ::: ::: Nodes with no edges at all have degree `0`, so an all-isolated graph is 0-regular but nothing else: ::: {#4d918690 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_node(label="A") graph.add_node(label="B") graph.add_node(label="C") graph.is_k_regular(0), graph.is_k_regular(1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (True, False) ``` ::: :::
